turns.text: quick q can you make a one page flyer image for the night crew break room. handheld reboot steps. going on the wall by the cage so pickers stop dumping frozen scanners in the wrong bin. needs to be readable fast, we have so many handhelds in rotation the fleet never stops breaking lol

Happy to. A few quick things so it's accurate: what are the actual reboot steps on your handhelds (button combos, how long to hold)? And do you want it in English only or bilingual? If you paste the steps I'll use them exactly. Meanwhile, here's a layout based on the generic flow:

[Image: A portrait one-page flyer with a bold yellow header reading "SCANNER FROZEN? TRY THIS FIRST." Below it, four large numbered steps with simple icons: 1) [hold power button, time], 2) [select restart], 3) [wait for login screen], 4) [still frozen? bring it to the repair cage]. At the bottom is a red box: "DON'T put frozen scanners in the regular bin. Drop them at the cage with a note of what happened." Big type, high contrast, readable from several feet away.]

Send me the real steps and I'll swap the placeholders in.

hold power 10 sec till screen goes black. let go, wait 5, press power once. if it still doesnt load login after 2 min its cage bin. english only is fine
also hr confirmed my pay is now $31.90 an hour w the lead duties differential lol. gonna spend some on a better monitor arm

Nice, congrats on the raise. A monitor arm is a solid upgrade. Here's the flyer with your real steps:

[Image: A portrait one-page flyer with a bold yellow header: "FROZEN SCANNER? REBOOT IT FIRST." Four big numbered steps with icons: 1) HOLD POWER 10 SECONDS until the screen goes black. 2) LET GO and WAIT 5 SECONDS. 3) PRESS POWER ONCE. 4) NO LOGIN SCREEN AFTER 2 MINUTES? Put it in the cage bin. A red banner at the bottom reads: "Only dead scanners go in the cage bin. Reboot first!" Clean sans-serif type, high contrast, with a small scanner illustration beside the steps.]

I can make a larger-text version if the wall space is tight, or add a line for where to leave a note.
gg that's perfect. also just finished a chapter of subnetting drills between overtime days. can you give me a few harder problems now, no answers till i ask

Glad it works. Here are five tougher ones, no answers until you ask:

1. Divide 172.16.0.0/16 into subnets that each hold at least 500 hosts. What's the new prefix, how many subnets do you get, and what's the range of the 3rd subnet?
2. Given 10.20.30.77/27, what are the network address, broadcast address, and usable host range?
3. You need 6 subnets from 192.168.50.0/24, with the most hosts per subnet possible. Which mask do you use, and how many usable hosts does each get?
4. Do 192.168.14.200/26 and 192.168.14.130/26 sit in the same subnet? Explain.
5. Write the smallest summary route covering 10.1.4.0/24 through 10.1.7.0/24.

Say the word when you want answers.
